newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade down on blue chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade down on blue chip losses.

text.p: Shares of Lever Brothers Nigeria Plc tumbled on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday on heavy selling, lowering the all-share index with it, traders.
The index was down 10.21 at 6690.63 from Monday's 6700.84 as investors continued to sell shares of the conglomerate and other blue chips.
Lever Brothers, the largest firm on the stock market by market capitalisation, fell 60 kobo to 23.90 naira.
The bearish sentiment also hit Cadbury's shares despite announcing an improved third quarter result last Friday.
It fell 17 kobo to 25.50 naira. Guinness was worse off, falling 29 kobo or the maximum five percent allowed daily, to 5.66 naira.
Flour Mills shares ended unchanged even though its mid-year profit after tax to end-September rose slightly to 152 million naira from 137.9 million naira last year.

Some key bank shares ended lower, also helping to depress the market. Guaranty Trust Bank was 13.40 naira, 10 kobo lower, while NAL Merchant Bank and Union Bank each shed five kobo each to 5.05 naira and 6.35 naira, respectively.
Nigerian Breweries, Union Dicon Salt and the actively traded oil marketing stocks, however, closed stronger on rising demand.
The brewer added 30 kobo to 13.50 naira while the salt firm finished 40 kobo more at 40.00 naira.
National Oil was just 10 kobo up after disappointing with a decline in its after-tax profit for the first half of the year.
It said net profit for the period to end-June fell to 463 million naira from 730 million naira in the same period last year.
African Petroleum was up 25 kobo to 38.30 naira and Total was 52.20 naira, 20 kobo higher. Agip was 12 kobo better at 17.32 naira while Mobil gained 10 kobo to 44.10 naira. ($1=80 naira)
